record.title: 22x16x4 bearing seated by interference — Ø16 inner ring on a printed boss, Ø22 outer ring in a printed bore

joins.a: the 22x16x4 ball bearing (part:bearing-22x16x4), interface 'bore' (Ø16.0, inner ring) or 'od' (Ø22.0, outer ring) — dimensions measured off Pollen's own mesh, no vendor designation exists in the reference
joins.b: the seat: a Ø16 boss for the inner ring (interface 'shaft'/'boss' — yaw2roll 'yaw_bearing_seat' Ø16.0 x 1.95 with its own Ø19.0 x 0.5 shoulder, hip-bracket 'roll_/pitch_bearing_seat' Ø16.0 x 1.95, yaw-roll-motion 'roll_bearing_seat' Ø16.0 x 4.0) or a Ø22 bore for the outer ring ('housing_bore'/'pocket' — trunk_base for hip-yaw, the head for head-roll); the microduck shelf's roles 'bearing_seat'/'bearing_face' also serve

record.dof_left_why: The joint this folder describes is the SEAT, and a seat leaves nothing free: an interference fit is a rigid connection. The one rotational DOF listed is the BEARING's, not the seat's — it is why the bearing is there at all: eleven placements, and the hip-yaw, hip-roll, hip-pitch, head-yaw and head-roll axes all turn on this ring opposite their servo horns (spec/mesh-placements.json). mate() returns rotation_about_z when the mated pair spans the bearing and [] for a single seat considered alone, and says which case it decided in the returned why.dof. Same split as connection:press-fit-608 and press-fit-bearing-15x10x3.
record.detachable_why: Detachable with a press or a puller. The press-fit-608 warning is inherited: pressing on the wrong ring drives the load through the balls and brinells the races. These seats are printed PLA, so disassembly is likelier to yield the plastic than the ring — also unmeasured.
record.standard: ISO 286-1 (limits and fits — the k6/h6/H7 grading compat.py can do WHEN a class is declared) / ISO 286-2 (the published tables; IT7 transcribed where it drifts from the formula, see why)
record.standard_why: ISO 286 defines the only fit language compat.py grades in, and its limits are DERIVED from ISO 286-1's own formulae — reproducing the published 16 k6 (+1/+12), 16 h6 (-11/0) and 22 k6 (+2/+15) exactly. The published IT7 at 10-18 (18 um) sits 1 um above raw 16i (17.32) — the same table drift press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 measured — so it is TRANSCRIBED in compat.PUBLISHED_IT7_UM with the drift recorded (at 18-30 the formula's 20.93 rounds to the published 21 on its own). The standard governs the GRADING VOCABULARY only: the reference design's actual seats are FDM PLA and carry no class, so the folder's fit verdict on those pairs is per-measurement, not per-class.
record.adds_parts_why: An interference fit adds no fastener; it adds the bearing itself, because a connection that seats a bearing is the reason the bearing appears in the BOM (the press-fit-608 rule). part:bearing-22x16x4 resolves on this shelf (checked 2026-09-02). No circlip is ever added: no circlip groove exists on any measured microduck seat and no circlip folder is on this shelf — mate() refuses the option by name rather than dangling a ref.
record.why: The GEOMETRY of the joint is PASS and it is measured on both sides: the ring is Ø16.0 bore / Ø22.0 OD / 4.0 wide (cecad.meshfeatures + bbox on seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4.stl, 2026-09-02, frozen in evidence/bearing-22x16x4-geometry.json, 11 placements), and the reference design's own seats measure at the same nominal — yaw2roll, hip-bracket and yaw-roll-motion bosses all Ø16.0, yaw2roll's with its own measured Ø19.0 x 0.5 shoulder sitting dead centre of the Ø16..Ø22 abutment band (each quoted in that part's own interfaces.json). What stays CANNOT DETERMINE is stated per-check and as ledger rows: the INTERFERENCE — printed PLA seats have no ISO class and the unnamed ring no vendor sheet, so grip and press force wait on calipers (measured_d_mm on the seat, ring_deviation_um on the ring); and the PARTIAL ENGAGEMENT — the 1.95 mm bosses carry the 4 mm ring at ~49% so the ring can span the joint gap to the mating part, which is Pollen's own design and a bench question, reported with its ratio and refused both verdicts. compat.py grades what can be graded and refuses the rest by name.

joint.default_state: the mated pair SPANS the bearing — a boss in the bore while a housing holds the OD (the hip-yaw / hip-roll / hip-pitch / head-yaw / head-roll idler side). mate() returns [] for a single seat alone and says which case it decided in why.dof.
joint.why: TWO holds_by values live in this folder, the press-fit-608 split kept verbatim: the SEAT is held by FRICTION (the interference) and leaves nothing free; the ROTATION is held by FORM, by the rolling elements, and lives ACROSS the two seats. This block describes the spanning case, which is what dof_left describes, so holds_by is form; mate() on a single seat returns all locked with holds_by 'friction' and says so. driven false: every one of the eleven placements is the IDLER side of an axis whose torque enters through the servo horn on the opposite face — a walk that read a driven joint off a bearing seat would double-drive the axis. rating: ring dimensions MEASURED (meshfeatures); grip_N and reference_speed_rpm MISSING — no vendor sheet exists for this unnamed ring and no bench has touched one here.
